edit.description: the pick range skips a commit the tip already holds, keyed on the sequencer state `cherryPickAbort` already probes for
the singleton leg's catch stops reading an emptied pick as a conflict
the per-entry leg does the same, and a span the tip holds whole carries with no commit to add
the primitive's skipped-commit and whole-span cases, beside the `cherryPickRange` block
both legs' reported facts, beside the cherry-pick-conflict cases

summary: A span the trunk already holds empties the pick, both merge legs read the throw as a conflict, and the tick counts errored toward the hibernate

per.section: Tip verify — one writer per branch, absorption at the merge

acceptance: a commit the tip already holds is skipped and the rest of the span lands; a span the tip holds whole merges with no commit to add, so the tick reports no commit landed and no merge failure and a fanout entry's `shipped` predicate is asked as for any merge; the evidence is git's own sequencer state, never its message, and no no-commit mode or merge outcome is added
tests: a span whose only commit the tip already holds merges with no commit to add and no merge failure
a span the tip holds one commit of skips that commit and lands the rest
a fanout entry whose span the tip already holds is asked for shipped as for any merge
notes: Operator's ruling on the field report (three times in one day, 0.19.0). `cherryPickRange` (`src/git.ts:299`) is a bare `cherry-pick base..head`; both callers read any throw as a conflict (`src/singletonTick.ts:379`, `src/waveMerge.ts`). `--empty=drop` is git 2.45 and the floor is 2.36, so the mechanism is the stopped sequencer with nothing staged plus `--skip` — the probe `cherryPickAbort` (`tests/git.test.ts:1008`) already spends.
